fact_check.claim: Access Fund open through April 15, 2027 (from Sept 21, 2026), reviewed rolling on the 15th of each month
fact_check.note: Page: Sept 21, 2026 to April 15, 2027; rolling review on the 15th of each month.

fact_check.claim: Basic Needs category provides cold weather coat, hat and gloves through the Cornell Store; decisions go to Cornell email, items provided through the Cornell Store (previous fix applied)
fact_check.note: Page: coat, hat, gloves provided through the Cornell Store; decisions sent to Cornell email. The article's softened wording matches.

fact_check.claim: Each Access Fund category needs its own application
fact_check.note: Page: separate application for each category.

fact_check.claim: Maximize Cornell: temporary laptop and cell phone replacement, career readiness attire, graduation expenses, gym membership for first-semester students only; no dollar cap listed
fact_check.note: Matches; page lists no cap for these.

fact_check.claim: Power of Experience pays up to $1,500 and requires resume, budget and alternative plan
fact_check.note: Page: up to $1,500; resume, confirmation of experience, alternative plan, proposed budget.

fact_check.claim: Undergraduates attach 2026-27 Financial Aid Summary; fund is not an emergency fund; eligibility is full-time undergraduate, graduate and professional students on the Ithaca campus with low or limited income and high financial need
fact_check.note: All stated on the page.

fact_check.claim: FGLI office in Barnes Hall Room 200, 607-254-1288, FGLIEmpowerment@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: Page: 200 Barnes Hall, (607) 254-1288, FGLIempowerment@cornell.edu (email case differs only).

fact_check.claim: Winter break housing $125 per one-week option, $500 full break; application open October 1, due December 1
fact_check.note: Page matches; it also says the fee text is jumbled and to confirm in the portal, which the article states.

fact_check.claim: Must be returning to on-campus housing for spring; non-residents only full break at $500 in limited flex spaces
fact_check.note: Page: returning for spring; very limited, Residential Flex Spaces in open buildings, full break only, $500.

fact_check.claim: HILC/Low Rise 8 and Loving House residents stay free; Veterans House residents free because included in academic-year license (previous fix applied; 'funded by individual gifts' removed)
fact_check.note: Page matches; no unsupported funding claim remains.

fact_check.claim: Fall meal plans end with the semester
fact_check.note: Page: fall meal plans end with the semester and do not carry over.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Dining closed Dec 25, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027; fall BRBs at open cafés through Dec 24 and Jan 4 to 19; City Bucks for off-campus meals or groceries
fact_check.note: All dates match.

fact_check.claim: Swipe Out Hunger fall 2026 runs Sept 21 to Dec 8; FGLI office is contact for urgent food needs
fact_check.note: Page matches. The article calls it temporary support for food-insecure students; the page describes donated bonus meals for food-insecure classmates. Close enough.

fact_check.claim: Big Red Basics: free cabinet of hygiene items, 206 Willard Straight Hall, Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-7 p.m., no appointment
fact_check.note: Page matches.

fact_check.claim: Books and course materials $1,234 and personal expenses $2,182 a year not billed; article says 'when we checked in November 2026'
fact_check.note: The figures are on the page, but they are the 2025-26 amounts; the 2026-27 table shows none. The figures are dated by the source and the page normally works, so this is acceptable, but the year label is imprecise.

fact_check.claim: Transportation listed as 'Varies', footnote says costs to and from campus vary by region
fact_check.note: Page matches.

fact_check.claim: Student Health Plan excluded from need-based aid estimate; optional costs and the plan not eligible for need-based grant aid; can request loan funding
fact_check.note: Page: SHP excluded because not charged to all; optional course fees, gym, premium housing and SHP not eligible for need-based grant aid; loan funding can be requested.

fact_check.claim: 2025-26 Student Health Plan $3,685 new, $4,020 returning, waiver due July 31
fact_check.note: Sun reports those prices and a July 31 waiver deadline for 2025-26. It is a newspaper source but is labeled 2025-26 with a check-current-year warning.

fact_check.claim: Michelle Van-Ess Grant, senior associate dean of students, said books, travel, professional clothing and basic needs can weigh heavily on first-gen and low-income students
fact_check.note: Sun names her with that title; she wrote that books, travel, professional clothing and even basic needs can weigh heavily. Paraphrased.

fact_check.claim: FirstGen Forward summary of uAspire: indirect expenses are more than half the cost of college and colleges often do not tell students
fact_check.note: Page says more than half of the cost and that colleges 'fail to give' students the information; credited to uAspire. 'Often do not tell' is a slight softening.

fact_check.claim: 2018 Cornell Chronicle feature notes low-income students may not be able to go home over breaks or may worry about food when dining hours shrink; Clency no longer credited (previous fix applied)
fact_check.note: Article dated Oct 30, 2018 describes those stresses; the article's wording now stays within it and does not attribute work to Clency.

fact_check.claim: 2021 Sun: aid packages do not adjust for international flights; some students go years between visits home
fact_check.note: Dec 7, 2021 article says aid is not adjusted for travel costs and quotes a student on years between visits.

fact_check.claim: Work-study capped at $1,300 per semester at the time; on-campus work limited for international students
fact_check.note: Article states the $1,300 per semester cap and the on-campus work limits; the article dates it (2021) and tells readers to ask Financial Aid.

fact_check.claim: Rafael Bitanga '23 said resources still feel limited in times of need; guide planned sections on employment, scholarships, housing, textbooks, clothing, food and study abroad
fact_check.note: Sun (March 28, 2021) matches both. This is student voice, paraphrased and attributed, not a hard fact.

beats_top.query: cornell first-gen low income hidden costs
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2018 Chronicle feature about the first-gen experience with no cost list, dates, or application steps. Ours puts the gaps first, gives current dates and fees, and says what to do in order.
